record.original_question: Which covariant classical theory of gravity is selected by the requirement that observed Schwarzschild and Newtonian exterior behavior be recovered: the Ricci-flat second-order Einstein theory, or a higher-derivative theory whose equations also admit Ricci-flat solutions but may have additional solutions? Answering this requires identifying the non-Schwarzschild solutions of higher-derivative gravity theories and determining their observational implications.

evidence.quote: Now it was noted by Eddington in the very early days of Relativity that this same exterior non-relativistic and relativistic phenomenology would follow if some other function of the Ricci tensor vanished, either a higher power of it or some derivative of it instead, since such a situation would still admit of the vanishing of the Ricci tensor itself.

With this being precisely the case which occurs in fourth order theories of gravity (theories which are just as covariant as the second order one), Eddington then threw out a challenge to the community to tell him which one the correct theory of gravity was.
This question has generally been ignored by the community and never satisfactorily resolved, even though it goes to the very heart of the question of the uniqueness of gravitational theory.

While the vanishing of a derivative or a higher power of the Ricci tensor implies the vanishing of the Ricci tensor, the reverse is not true, since the vanishing of a function of the Ricci tensor could have other, possibly less desirable solutions as well, and thus in order to answer Eddington’s question it is necessary to find such other solutions and identify their observational implications.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider covariant classical theories of gravity in four-dimensional spacetime whose field equations admit every Ricci-flat metric (so in particular the Schwarzschild metric) as a solution, thereby reproducing the standard Newtonian and Schwarzschild exterior phenomenology in the appropriate regimes. Two natural candidates are:

(a) The second-order Einstein theory, whose vacuum field equations are R_{μν} = 0.

(b) A higher-derivative theory of gravity, for example one derived from a Lagrangian of the form L = √(-g)(α R^2 + β R_{μν} R^{μν} + γ R_{μνρσ} R^{μνρσ}) or more generally one whose vacuum equations take the form F_{μν}(R_{αβ}, ∇R_{αβ}, ∇∇R_{αβ}, …) = 0 where F vanishes whenever R_{αβ} = 0. Such a theory admits all Ricci-flat metrics as solutions but may admit additional, non-Ricci-flat vacuum solutions.

Determine, on the basis of observational consequences, which of these covariant theories of gravity is selected by the requirement that the exterior gravitational phenomenology of an isolated spherical body match the observed Schwarzschild/Newtonian behavior. Specifically:

(i) Classify all static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat vacuum solutions of the higher-derivative theory (b) that are not Ricci-flat (in particular, the non-Schwarzschild branch).

(ii) Determine the observational signatures of these additional solutions (e.g. modifications to the exterior metric, perihelion precession, light bending, thermodynamics of black holes), and decide whether their existence can be reconciled with, or is excluded by, observations, thereby resolving whether the second-order Einstein theory is uniquely selected among such covariant theories.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on part (i): Lü, Perkins, Pope and Stelle (2015) demonstrated, both via a Lichnerowicz-type theorem and numerically, the existence of a non-Schwarzschild branch of static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat black-hole solutions in four-dimensional Einstein gravity supplemented by quadratic curvature terms, with vanishing Ricci scalar. Subsequent works (e.g. Kokkotas–Konoplya–Zhidenko 2017) provided accurate analytical approximations and studied their stability, quasinormal modes and thermodynamics, and further novel families have been constructed (e.g. 2023 results in JHEP). However, a complete classification of all non-Schwarzschild solutions and a definitive observational verdict deciding Eddington's uniqueness challenge in favor of one theory has not been established; the broader question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Black Holes in Higher-Derivative Gravity (Lü, Perkins, Pope, Stelle)
status_evidence.snippet: Static black-hole solutions in Einstein gravity with additional quadratic curvature terms; existence of non-Schwarzschild black holes shown numerically; Lichnerowicz-type theorem implies vanishing Ricci scalar.
status_evidence.claim: Non-Schwarzschild branch of black-hole solutions in quadratic gravity has been established.

status_evidence.title: Non-Schwarzschild black-hole metric in four-dimensional higher derivative gravity: analytical approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Continued-fraction analytic approximation of the numerical non-Schwarzschild solution; analysis of thermodynamics, geodesics, perturbations and quasinormal spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Observational and dynamical properties of the non-Schwarzschild solution are being computed.

status_evidence.title: Novel black holes in higher derivative gravity (JHEP 02 (2023) 057)
status_evidence.snippet: Further new black-hole solutions in higher-derivative gravity beyond Schwarzschild.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of non-Schwarzschild solutions is still being extended.
